correctness.rationale: A non-ultimately-periodic word has a right-special factor at every n, otherwise length-n windows evolve deterministically in a finite state space. Complement closure gives a distinct complementary right-special factor, hence p(n+1)-p(n)>=2 and p(n)>=2n. At odd n, complementation freely pairs any coordinate-permutation orbit classes because their Hamming weights differ, giving even class counts. p_ab<=n+1 then forces p_ab+1<2n<=p for odd n>=3. Exhaustive independently enumerated S3 subgroup and Thue–Morse factor checks matched the six subgroup values; this is not the infinite proof.

final_claim: Every non-ultimately-periodic binary infinite word with complement-closed full factor language has p_x(n)>=2n for every n>=1, and for every odd length n all coordinate-permutation subgroup orbit counts are even. Thus p_ab(n)+1 is an omitted strict intermediate value at each odd n>=3; length 3 is the first possible obstruction for any binary word. For Thue–Morse the S3 subgroup spectrum at length 3 is {2:2,4:3,6:1}.
